concepts.for_persona_or_act: QA, the settlement suite that passed because fixtures and code shared one reading of the spec
concepts.diagram_type: causal provenance graph with a shared-ancestor wedge, and a second root feeding an independent oracle
concepts.what_it_shows: Ticket text branching into implementation and fixtures, with the assertion drawn as an edge between two siblings inside a wedge that makes their common parent visible. A separate root, the merchant agreement, descends through a reference implementation and enters the same comparison from outside the wedge.
concepts.why_this_shape: The question a senior reviewer asks is where the expected value came from, which is an ancestry question. Only a graph can show that a test compares two descendants of the same misreading. A before and after would compare two suites and say nothing about why the green one is worthless.
concepts.layout_spec: viewBox 0 0 640 300. Root A: rect 250,24 w150 h30, 'ticket text'. Children: rect 160,104 w150 h34 'implementation'; rect 380,104 w160 h34 'fixtures, expected values'. Edges from root A bottom centre (325,54) to each child top centre. Wedge: dotted path from 325,54 down to 150,150 across to 550,150 and back, opacity 0.4, no fill, label at 350,166 centred 11px 'one parent'. Assertion: horizontal double-headed arrow y=192 from 235,192 to 460,192, label centred at 347,186 'assert equal' (11px). Root B: rect 30,24 w150 h30 'merchant agreement'; rect 20,104 w130 h34 'reference impl'; vertical edge between them; then a path from 85,138 down to 85,192 and right to 235,192 joining the assertion, drawn at stroke-width 2, label at 96,210 'independent oracle' (11px). Inputs: rect 250,236 w170 h30 'restored 90-day snapshot' with two arrows up-left to the reference impl and up-right to the implementation, single shared label at 430,254, 11px opacity 0.65: 'same inputs, different lineage'.
concepts.caption_argument: An oracle is only worth what its ancestry is worth. Two artefacts generated in one pass from one prompt cannot disagree about the thing the prompt got wrong, however many assertions sit between them.

concepts.for_persona_or_act: QA, what the diff-level gate actually admits
concepts.diagram_type: coverage versus mutation quadrant with an L-shaped admissible corner and a decay vector
concepts.what_it_shows: Modules plotted on branch coverage against mutation score, both measured on the diff. Two dashed thresholds cut the plane, and only the top-right corner merges. The settlement aggregation sits far right and low, at ninety-four percent coverage with surviving mutants on the day boundary, and an arrow shows a module drifting into that corner over six months of quarantine.
concepts.why_this_shape: Coverage and mutation are two independent measurements of the same suite, so the natural object is a plane, and the interesting fact is a whole populated region rather than one comparison. The gate being a corner rather than a line is a claim you can only draw in two dimensions.
concepts.layout_spec: viewBox 0 0 640 320. Axes in currentColor: x axis y=270 from x=60 to x=590 with arrowhead, label at 325,296 centred 'branch coverage on the diff' (11px); y axis x=60 from y=270 to y=40 with arrowhead, label rotated -90 at 26,155 'mutation score on the diff' (11px). Dashed threshold lines: vertical x=430 from y=270 to y=40 labelled at 434,36 '80%' (10px); horizontal y=120 from x=60 to x=590 labelled at 44,124 '70%' (10px). Admissible region: rect 430,40 w160 h80 drawn at stroke-width 2 with 45 degree hatch at 10px pitch, opacity 0.3, label centred at 510,86 'merges' (11px). Points as circles r4 with 11px labels offset 8px: A at 476,80 'money rules'; B at 512,214 'settlement agg'; C at 200,96 'date utils'; D at 152,238 'reporting views'. Callout from B: leader to 400,240, text 'two mutants live on the day boundary' (11px). Decay vector: curved arrow from 470,92 to 520,200 with arrowhead at the lower end, label at 540,150 'six months of quarantine' set on two lines (11px). Quadrant note at 480,258, 11px opacity 0.65: 'executed, not checked'.
concepts.caption_argument: Coverage tells you a line ran. The bottom-right of this plane is full of suites that ran everything and can disagree with nothing, and it is where a quarantine list quietly moves your riskiest module.

concepts.for_persona_or_act: technical BA, three departments and three true definitions of active account
concepts.diagram_type: definition space lattice: grain on one axis, as-of semantics on the other, with the merged term drawn as a point that cannot exist
concepts.what_it_shows: Three stakeholder definitions placed in a nine-cell grid of population by time semantics, each one internally valid and none adjacent. The single column everyone asked for is drawn at the centroid as a struck-through hollow circle. Beneath, the resolution: three named metrics and one shared conformed dimension.
concepts.why_this_shape: The finding is that the disagreement has two independent dimensions, so a list, a table of definitions, or a with and without pair all flatten exactly the thing being discovered. Placing the three claims in a plane makes the distance between them the argument and makes the compromise position visibly empty.
concepts.layout_spec: viewBox 0 0 640 320. Grid: three column centres x = 170, 340, 510 with light vertical guides from y=60 to y=250 at opacity 0.3; three row centres y = 90, 160, 230 with light horizontal guides x=100 to x=580. Column headers at y=48, centred, 11px: 'login identity', 'account', 'parent entity'. Row labels right-aligned at x=94, 11px, two lines each: 'trailing 30d sessions', 'rolling 90d usage', 'as-of close, restatable'. Filled dots r5: Growth at 170,90; Customer Success at 510,160; Finance at 340,230, each with an 11px label offset up-left by 10px. Impossible point: hollow circle r9 at 340,160 with a diagonal slash across it, leader line to 420,132, label 'one column called active account' set on two lines (11px). Resolution row: three chips, rect w160 h26 at y=272, x = 60, 240, 420, 11px centred: 'active_login_30d', 'active_usage_90d', 'active_contract_asof'. Shared bar: rect 60,304 w520 h14, 11px centred inside 'account-month dimension'.
concepts.caption_argument: Three people were right and the word was wrong. Once the disagreement is plotted rather than debated, the answer stops being a compromise definition and becomes three names and one shared dimension.

concepts.for_persona_or_act: technical BA, the rule to test to merge chain and where it breaks
concepts.diagram_type: four-column traceability web carrying three different kinds of break, with the healthy chains dropped back in weight
concepts.what_it_shows: Rules, stories, tests and merged commits linked as a web. Three defects are drawn at full strength while everything correct sits at low opacity: one chain whose final link ends in mid-air, one complete chain whose test has never once gone red, and one rule with no example at all.
concepts.why_this_shape: Traceability decay is a property of links, and links have no representation in a comparison of two states. Drawing the whole web and then de-emphasising the healthy paths reproduces the actual review experience, where the defect is an absence you have to hunt for rather than a difference you can point at.
concepts.layout_spec: viewBox 0 0 640 300. Column headers at y=26, 11px opacity 0.65, centred on x = 80, 250, 420, 570: 'rule', 'story', 'test', 'merged'. Rule nodes: rect w90 h26 at x=35, y = 60, 110, 160, 210, labelled R-11 to R-14. Story nodes: rect w110 h26 at x=195, y = 50, 95, 140, 185. Test nodes: rect w110 h26 at x=365, y = 50, 95, 140, 185. Commit nodes: rect w80 h26 at x=530, y = 62, 112, 170. Edges are thin quadratic curves between node right and left edges. All healthy nodes and edges at opacity 0.4. Defect 1: R-13 chain drawn at opacity 1, its test to commit edge starts at 475,153 and terminates at 512,150 in an open circle r4 with no target, label at 500,176, 11px, 'dangling'. Defect 2: R-12 chain at opacity 1 with a hollow square 9x9 at 358,88 on its test node, note at 365,32 wait no, place note under the test node at 365,122, 11px: 'never red, 90 days'. Defect 3: R-14 rect at opacity 1 with no outgoing edge at all, and a short label at 132,224, 11px: 'no example'.
concepts.caption_argument: A missing link raises no error anywhere, and a link that exists is not a link that fires. Both of these read as a shorter report rather than as broken instrumentation.

concepts.for_persona_or_act: team shape, one week on an eleven-person team converging on a single merge
concepts.diagram_type: role swimlanes across five days funnelling into one merge node, with one work item ejected back
concepts.what_it_shows: Six role lanes across Monday to Friday. A design note lands before any branch exists, a migration runs both directions against a restored copy, an ADR supersedes another and its fitness function ships in evaluate mode, four stacked pull requests and a second derivation that disagrees by 0.4 percent, then a merge queue node that takes three and returns one for a stale base.
concepts.why_this_shape: The claim is that eleven people and five days converge on one point, and convergence is a shape. A before and after cannot show sequence, ownership and one item travelling backwards at the same time. The funnel plus the single deflected line is what makes the merge queue's job visible.
concepts.layout_spec: viewBox 0 0 640 340. Day gridlines at x = 120, 220, 320, 420, 520 from y=34 to y=286, opacity 0.25; day labels centred at y=24, 11px: Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri. Six lanes with left labels right-aligned at x=104, 11px, baselines y = 56, 96, 136, 176, 216, 256: principal, tech BA, data eng, backend, QA, platform. Glyph vocabulary, stated once by shape not colour: rounded rect equals vault note, circle equals pull request, small triangle equals a check result, square equals a policy rule. Mon: rounded rect 132,44 w76 h24 spanning down to a second at 132,84 joined by a left bracket, single label at 132,118, 11px, 'design note, no branch'. Tue: circle r8 at 244,136 'draft PR' labelled at 256,132; triangle side 12 at 272,156 with label 'fwd and reverse on restored copy' set on two lines at 232,180, 11px. Wed: rounded rect 332,44 w80 h24, label 'ADR-0042 supersedes 0031' on two lines at 332,84; square 12x12 at 344,250 label 'fitness fn, evaluate' at 360,254. Thu: four circles r6 at 436,166 / 452,166 / 468,166 / 484,166, label 'four stacked PRs' at 430,146; two converging arrows into a diamond at 452,216, label '0.4% disagreement' at 400,238. Fri: thin lines from every glyph converging into a hexagon centred 596,150 r22 drawn at stroke-width 2, label 'merge queue' at 560,120. One circle from Thu deflects: curved arrow from 484,166 out to 596,150 and back left to 508,196 with arrowhead, label 'ejected, stale base' at 470,214, 11px.
concepts.caption_argument: The week's output is not a feature. It is a reversibility proof, a superseded decision, an advisory rule with a promotion date, a 0.4 percent disagreement someone chased, and one pull request the queue refused.

concepts.for_persona_or_act: team shape, which artefact lives in the vault and which lives in the repository
concepts.diagram_type: two-basin loop with a gate on the isthmus and a mechanical check on each direction of travel
concepts.what_it_shows: Two containers with their real contents listed, a narrow channel between them carrying a gate glyph, one arc across labelled binding and one arc back labelled pointer rather than copy. A check marker sits on each arc: a schema change without a contract update fails the build, a dangling ADR reference fails the link check.
concepts.why_this_shape: The question is not which tool is better, it is where a given artefact belongs and what enforces the boundary. Two basins joined by a narrow channel says containment and passage in one figure, and putting the checks physically on the arcs answers the question a comparison cannot: what happens mechanically when the two disagree.
concepts.layout_spec: viewBox 0 0 640 300. Left container: rounded rect 30,50 w250 h200 rx=12, title at 44,72, 12px, 'vault, git-backed'; five 11px lines at 44,100 with 20px leading, opacity 0.8: 'interview notes', 'half-formed models', 'open questions', 'on-call handovers', 'incident timelines'. Right container: rounded rect 360,50 w250 h200 rx=12, title at 374,72, 'repository'; five 11px lines at 374,100 with 20px leading: 'ADRs', 'feature files', 'data contracts', 'diagrams as code', 'migration and reverse'. Isthmus: two short vertical bars at x=316 and x=326, y 118 to 152, with a 10px gap between them, label centred above at 321,108, 11px, 'graduates when a build depends on it' set on two lines. Top arc: path from 280,96 curving up through 320,74 into 360,96 with an arrowhead, label at 321,60, 11px, 'binding'. Bottom arc: path from 360,214 curving down through 320,238 into 280,214 with an arrowhead, dashed (5,3), label at 321,258, 11px, 'pointer, never a copy'. Check markers: triangle side 11 at 300,80 with label at 312,84, 11px, 'schema change without contract fails'; triangle side 11 at 340,232 with label at 352,236, 11px, 'dangling ADR fails'.
concepts.caption_argument: The vault holds thinking and the repository holds anything a build depends on. That split is only real if something mechanical fails when the two drift, which is the pair of triangles on the arcs.

concepts.for_persona_or_act: team shape, where the four gates actually fire in the life of a pull request
concepts.diagram_type: pull request event axis with gates hung above the event that triggers them, and a band marking the only event that tests the trunk as merged
concepts.what_it_shows: Five events along a pull request's life, from local commit to post-merge, with each gate attached by a stem to the event that actually fires it. The numbers gate sits on push, the migration gate on open, the ran gate and the approval gate on merge_group, and a hatched band marks merge_group as the only point where the branch is tested as it will exist after the queue.
concepts.why_this_shape: Gates are usually drawn as a checklist, which implies they all fire at the same moment and cost the same. An event axis forces each gate to declare when it runs, exposes that the merge_group build is the one nobody wires up, and lets the cost ramp sit underneath as a second reading.
concepts.layout_spec: viewBox 0 0 640 300. Event axis line y=150, x 40 to 610, with arrowhead. Five event ticks (vertical 12px through the axis) at x = 70, 190, 310, 440, 560; labels below at y=176, centred, 11px, two lines where needed: 'local commit', 'PR opened', 'each push', 'merge_group', 'post-merge'. Gate chips are rects h=22 with 11px centred text, each joined to its event by a vertical stem: at x=70, chip y=110 w120 'lint, secret scan'; at x=190, chip y=112 w120 'codeowner routing' and chip y=76 w170 'migration: fwd and reverse on a restored copy' (two lines, h=34); at x=310, chip y=108 w180 'numbers: second derivation vs pinned snapshot' (two lines, h=34); at x=440, chip y=110 w190 'ran: exit 0 and nonzero duration', chip y=70 w150 'approval: signed trailer'; at x=560, chip y=110 w120 'drift and traffic evidence'. Band: rect 412,40 w62 h170 with 45 degree hatch at 9px pitch, opacity 0.28, no outline except a 1px dashed left and right edge, label centred above at 443,32, 11px, 'trunk as merged, tested only here'. Cost ramp: filled-free wedge polygon from 40,214 to 610,214 to 610,242 to 40,228, opacity 0.35, with 'cheap' at 44,258 and 'expensive' at 606,258 right-aligned, both 11px.
concepts.caption_argument: A gate that is not attached to an event is a wish. Put each one on the event that fires it and the shape of the pipeline changes: the two gates that decide whether the trunk survives both live at merge_group, which is the build most teams never subscribe to.
